label: Fullscreen Modal
title: Fullscreen Modal
summary: Use a Fullscreen Modal for a focused, full-screen moment, such as an upgrade offer, with a hero, details, and one main action.
corePrinciple: One big moment, one main action, and always a way out.

anatomy.title: Hero text, a body, a footer, and a close button
anatomy.description: Centred hero text sits at the bottom of a space reserved for hero media, on the modal’s own black surface. Your Sections follow and scroll; the footer stays at the bottom with the main button, and a close button floats top right.

configuration.title: Hero, body, and footer
configuration.description: Set the hero copy, add Sections for the details, and choose the footer’s button and disclaimer. Hero media fills the width behind the hero text, and heroHeight sets how much space the text sits at the bottom of.

states.title: Shown until the screen removes it
states.description: Fullscreen Modal has no open or closed state. The screen shows it and removes it; its close button and main button only report the press.

sizing.title: The whole screen
sizing.description: Fullscreen Modal fills its screen and scrolls inside it. The hero text sits at the bottom of a 532 px space by default, the body starts 16 px below it with 16 px between Sections, and the footer stays at the bottom. The close button is 28 px, 12 px from the top and right.

content.title: An offer in four lines and one action
content.description: Use the eyebrow for the product or offer, the headline for the benefit in a few words, one supporting sentence, and the price on its own line. Label the button with the action. A line you leave unset doesn’t show.

sources.title: Use the public Fullscreen Modal contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build) from the team’s private package repository. In Figma the modal is 1228 px tall with a full-height image behind everything; in the package it has its own black surface, so the hero text reads without media, and media you add sits behind the hero and the body. As in Figma, its hero space is 532 px and its close button 28 px. The close button shows only when the screen handles it, and copy you leave unset stays empty. On the web it’s a dialog named by its headline, which is a heading. When it has a close button, focus moves to its scrolling body, Tab cycles the body, the main button, and the close button, the arrow and Page keys scroll the body, Escape closes it, and focus returns when it’s removed. trapFocus= turns that off for a modal shown inside a page, as in these examples; In context, and the States example once you show it again, keep it. The published Storybook predates this build.
